basis: Purchase of a company that was already listed, with no Bessemer round before the listing (COLLECTION.md s1 T3, decisions.md R3): Centocor offered 'its stock to the public in 1982' (International Directory of Company Histories, on FundingUniverse) and the firm's own list dates its investment 1989, seven years after the listing, with no description of an earlier round.

Purchase of a company that was already listed, with no Bessemer round before the listing (COLLECTION.md s1 T3, decisions.md R3): Commercial Federal became 'a publicly traded, investor-owned institution' in 1984, with a national public offering completed that year (International Directory of Company Histories, on FundingUniverse), and the firm's own list dates its investment 1992, the year the holding company offered about $40M of new equity; no earlier round is recorded.

Purchase of a company that was already listed, with no Bessemer round before the listing (COLLECTION.md s1 T3, decisions.md R3): Ganesh Housing Corporation was a listed company by February 2007, when it allotted 7,000,000 shares to qualified institutional buyers under a QIP and awaited listing approval for them (Equity Bulls, 2007-02-14); the firm's own list dates the BVP India investment 2008-06-04.

Purchase of a company that was already listed, with no Bessemer round before the listing (COLLECTION.md s1 T3, decisions.md R3): the row is AIT Group plc, later Portrait Software. AIT's shares were suspended in June 2002 and on 2002-08-01 it agreed a secured rescue loan of 6M pounds 'provided by a combination of Bessemer Venture Partners', local private investors and its founder, with 'an option to convert the full amount of the loan into ordinary shares of AIT following shareholder approval' (Finextra, read in its archived copy); the firm's own list dates its investment 2002. A rescue financing of a listed company is not a venture round.

Purchase of a company that was already listed, with no Bessemer round before the listing (COLLECTION.md s1 T3, decisions.md R3): Riddhi Siddhi Gluco Biols 'came out with a public issue in Nov.93' (India Infoline company summary) and the firm's own list dates the BVP India investment 2006-12-29, thirteen years after the listing.

Purchase of a company that was already listed, with no Bessemer round before the listing (COLLECTION.md s1 T3, decisions.md R3): Tulip IT Services, later Tulip Telecom, closed its IPO in December 2005 and was 'Listed on Thu, Jan 5, 2006' on the BSE and NSE (Chittorgarh IPO record); the firm's own list, in its one capture of the row, dates the BVP India investment 2007.

Control position (COLLECTION.md s1 control positions, decisions.md R1; the Medi Assist and GTS precedents): the firm's own archived description says 'BVP participated in the 1980 transaction that spun Harco ... out of its corporate parent Beatrice Foods'. That transaction was the purchase of the business from Beatrice: 'In 1980 Sidney Harman and a group of investors paid $55 million' for it (International Directory of Company Histories, on FundingUniverse). The firm was in the group that bought the company, so there is no venture round. The listing check itself is clean: the company was private from 1980 to its 1986 IPO.

note: Listed-purchase check closed: OnMobile's IPO ran 24 to 29 January 2008 and the shares listed on 2008-02-19 (Chittorgarh IPO record), eight weeks after the firm's own investment date of 2007-12-27, so the entry is a pre-IPO placement in a company founded in 2000, a member at Growth (decisions.md R3).

Listed-purchase check closed: Shriram EPC listed on 2008-02-20 (Chittorgarh IPO record), two years after the firm's own investment date of 2006-03-27, and the firm's 2008 history page counts it among its India practice's 'growth equity investments in firms such as Motilal Oswal and Shriram EPC', so Growth.

The firm's own 2005 list: 'BVP's Chris Gabrieli invested in Allscript's second round in April 1988. The company went public in July 1999', so a private entry eleven years before the listing; a second round reads Growth and the date replaces the list's bare 1987.
